todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.
outcome: Finish task 004 by enforcing durable member/group cleanup for source-less raw follows on post-cleanup conversations and correctly ordering generation-less reply-author follows stored on reply streams.
scope: Revise the existing unaccepted task-004 candidate in place. Preserve its public Membership-to-Messaging cleanup collaboration, member and conversation cleanup facts, trusted current-member/root/reply source capture, generation-less manual/root compatibility, surviving-group behavior, and idempotent replay while addressing only the latest two review gaps.

Close the post-cleanup-conversation escape in raw `Memba.Messaging.follow_conversation/2`. `follow_conversation_command/1` now strips caller source and generation, but `ConversationFollowers` sees only its own conversation stream and a newly created conversation has no removal cutoff; ensure a source-less raw attempt also respects applicable durable `MemberFollowEligibility` member/group cleanup or is conservatively rejected.

Use the conversation's authoritative Messaging-owned access groups when an applicable group set is needed for the raw-follow cutoff decision. Do not trust caller-supplied `authorizing_group_ids`, do not infer renewed authority from the club-wide current generation, and do not let a later re-add retroactively activate a raw follow attempted while absent.

Add an integration regression for removal and completed cleanup, creation of a new conversation for the removed group while the member remains absent, a source-less raw follow attempt, and later re-add. Prove the raw attempt emits no `ConversationFollowed`, creates no projected follow, and causes no reply delivery after re-add; only a subsequent `follow_conversation_as_current_member/2` may restore follow state and normal reply delivery.

Extend the immutable-checkpoint compatibility path for historical generation-less reply-author follows. `latest_generationless_follow_checkpoint/2` currently filters to the root stream and `generationless_follow_fact?/3` accepts only root `MessageSent`, while historical replies are stored on their reply message streams and name the root in `conversation_id`; discover the actual reply fact without rewriting history or manufacturing a new follow.

For a generation-less reply `MessageSent` whose sender-follow semantics are active, remove its projected follow when the fact predates the historical removal, but preserve it when a matching durable group re-add lies between that removal checkpoint and the reply checkpoint. Persist the decision through Messaging-owned cleanup facts so first handling, retry, handler restart, aggregate restart, and full projection replay agree even though the root `ConversationFollowers` stream does not rehydrate reply-stream events.

Add focused pre-removal and post-re-add regressions using actual generation-less reply `MessageSent` shapes on reply streams. Assert event ordering, `ConversationUnfollowed.follow_retained`, projected state, notification eligibility, exact cleanup idempotency, restart behavior, and replay behavior; ensure non-following historical replies cannot create phantom follows.

Rerun the focused task-004 suites to preserve initially-unfollowed cleanup, manual/root/reply auto-follow cleanup, surviving-group same-generation causality, generated and historical post-re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, cleanup checkpoint interleaving, accepted task-001 removal behavior, and system-group no-ops.
scope_exclusions: Do not change task identity 004, reset the bounded revision count, or discard any of its seven cumulative candidate origins.
Do not restore trust in caller-supplied raw `authorizing_group_ids` or `membership_generation`, and do not let a source-less raw follow use an unrelated club membership generation as authorization.
Do not make re-add restore an old or absent-period follow. Re-add restores access and history only; a new authorized current-member follow is required to resume notifications.

Do not rewrite historical Membership or Messaging events, mutate foreign-context projections directly, or add a second cleanup process. Keep the collaboration through public bounded-context APIs and append-only Messaging facts.
Do not treat every reply as a follow: honor `MessageSent.sender_follows_conversation?/1`, the actual conversation/member identity, generation-less compatibility conditions, and immutable event order.

Do not weaken the effective-access union: a genuine follow or sender auto-follow authorized through surviving group B remains valid at group A's removal generation, while work sourced only from removed A remains rejected.
Do not change accepted task-001 custom-group removal authorization, transition/idempotency semantics, club roles or membership, last-member behavior, or system-group guards.

Do not implement current query/action authorization, LiveView refresh, queued provider-handoff, Leave/Remove UI, empty-group presentation, feature-file changes, or broader acceptance coverage assigned to tasks 009-016.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, browser acceptance, or another unscoped full-suite command; task 017 and the deterministic `dev_check` node own the final repository gate.

references.facts: Implementation Plan 2, the acceptance criteria, and Open Technical Decisions require public Messaging APIs, cleanup of manual and automatic follow sources, fresh opt-in after re-add, unrelated-follow preservation, and stale-safe durable ordering.
Iteration 062 established the replay-safe Membership-to-Messaging follow-cleanup boundary that explicit custom-group removal extends.
Membership owns membership facts, Messaging owns follows and delivery, and collaboration crosses public context APIs rather than direct foreign aggregate or projection writes.
Club history is authoritative for membership lifecycle, historical facts remain immutable/replayable, and system-group membership remains a policy consequence.
Command-side facts carry causal authority; query projections may support lookup but must not manufacture follow authorization.
Historical compatibility must be append-only, replayable, and tested against actual production-history event shapes.
Use deterministic process/checkpoint synchronization and avoid timing sleeps in ordering and restart regressions.

`follow_conversation_command/1` strips raw source and generation, while `follow_conversation_as_current_member/2` stamps authoritative groups and generation at a stable checkpoint. `establish_message_sender_follow/1` consults `MemberFollowEligibility`, but raw follows do not. `latest_generationless_follow_checkpoint/2` scans `$all` yet currently requires the recorded stream to equal the root conversation and recognizes only root-shaped `MessageSent` facts.

The member-scoped aggregate durably stores per-club/group cleanup generations specifically to protect conversations created after cleanup; its current public decision is used only by committed sender-follow work.

The root aggregate enforces conversation-local cutoffs and persists `ConversationUnfollowed.follow_retained`, but it rehydrates only events routed to the root stream and therefore does not see historical reply `MessageSent` facts stored on reply streams.

The follow projector treats historical generation-less root and reply `MessageSent` facts with active sender-follow semantics as projected follows and applies cleanup according to `follow_retained`; replay must preserve the same final state.

`conversation_id` identifies a reply's root, generation-less history predates sender membership generations, and `sender_follows_conversation?/1` is the compatibility predicate for whether the sender follows.

Existing integration coverage proves forged-source rejection only on a conversation that already has a local cleanup cutoff and proves generation-less manual/root ordering; add the post-cleanup new-conversation raw case and actual reply-stream historical cases.
Aggregate regressions cover retained cleanup and replay on the root stream; preserve them and add directly affected compatibility assertions where useful.

The current revise verdict identifies exactly two residual gaps: raw source-less follow acceptance for conversations created after member cleanup, and missing source-backed ordering for generation-less reply events stored outside the root stream.

constraints: Keep this as revision attempt eight for the same pending obligation and build on the current candidate rather than replacing its established behavior.

A source-less raw follow attempted after an applicable member/group cleanup must not create effective follow state, including when the conversation was created only after cleanup and has no conversation-local cutoff.

A genuine authorized current-member follow after re-add must continue deriving current readable groups and the current generation at the stable authorization checkpoint and must restore ordinary future notification eligibility.
Non-empty source attribution must continue to come only from authoritative current membership or a committed message event whose source was captured at that boundary.

Historical reply discovery must use immutable Messaging source facts and their global checkpoints, match the root conversation and member precisely, and require active sender-follow semantics; stream location alone is not conversation identity.

The compatibility decision must be persisted in Messaging-owned facts and remain identical on first cleanup, exact retry, handler/aggregate restart, and projection replay without requiring old reply facts to be copied into the root stream.

Preserve cleanup checkpoint synchronization, per-group and historic conversation cutoffs, member-scoped cleanup IDs, ordinary-unfollow history, public add/remove return modes, and Everyone/Admin behavior.
Keep edits limited to raw-follow cutoff enforcement, historical reply-source ordering, directly affected event/command compatibility if necessary, focused tests, and concise explanatory comments.
completion_evidence_required: List changed paths and identify how source-less raw follows now consult or conservatively honor durable member/group cleanup for conversations lacking a local cutoff, while trusted current-member, root, and reply paths retain authoritative source capture.

Identify the regression proving removal/cleanup, a newly created removed-group conversation, raw follow while absent, and re-add produce no `ConversationFollowed`, projected follow, or reply delivery until a new authorized current-member follow.

Describe how generation-less reply `MessageSent` facts are found across reply streams, matched to the root/member, ordered against removal and re-add checkpoints, and represented durably without rewriting history or manufacturing follows.

Identify regressions proving cleanup of a generation-less pre-removal reply-author follow and preservation of a generation-less post-re-add reply-author follow, including no-follow reply handling, exact retry, process restart, and projection/aggregate replay assertions.

Confirm prior manual/root/reply cleanup, surviving-group causality, generated and historical post-re-add behavior, unrelated-follow preservation, checkpoint interleaving, idempotency, and Everyone/Admin regressions remain passing.
Report exact exit statuses and test counts for both focused test commands, plus `git diff --check`, on the handoff state.

Confirm accepted task-001 behavior remains unchanged: explicit custom-group removal reuses `GroupMemberRemoved`, exact retry emits no new Membership fact, and club roles/membership plus system-group guards are preserved.

latest_review.summary: Raw source-less follows still bypass durable member cleanup on conversations created after cleanup because only the new conversation aggregate is checked; generation-less reply-author facts remain invisible to the root-stream compatibility scan and aggregate replay.

latest_worker_result.summary: The candidate removed generation inheritance from raw follows and added immutable-checkpoint ordering for generation-less manual/root facts, reporting 44 and 83 focused tests passing; review found the post-cleanup new-conversation and reply-stream branches still uncovered.
